idiom_name: domain objects (entities + value objects) with smart constructors and a mapping seam
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give every domain concept one type that owns both its data and the rules governing it - commands instead of setters, queries with domain meaning instead of raw getters - and create instances only through constructors or factories that establish the invariants (return a validation error rather than an invalid object). Give identity-bearing objects a stable id and equality by identity, make descriptive concepts immutable with equality by attributes, and let an aggregate root be the only entry point to a cluster that must stay consistent. Keep the model free of persistence, transport and presentation concerns; translate at the outer layer with mappers or repositories, and keep application concerns (transactions, authorization, workflow) in a thin Service Layer.
code_sketch:
order = Order.open(customer_id)      # smart constructor establishes the invariants
order.add_line(line)                 # command; rejects transitions that break rules
assert order.total() <= Order.LIMIT  # query with domain meaning, not a getter

# the outer layer owns persistence:
rows = mapper.to_rows(order)         # the mapper knows the model, not the reverse
pitfalls: Collapsing to one class per table, so the object graph mirrors the schema instead of the domain.
Letting persistence or serialization constraints (no-arg constructors, public fields, DTO shapes) dictate the model.
Drifting to either extreme: behaviourless entities (anemic) or entities that absorb every application use case (god object).
Creating oversized aggregates that span multiple bounded contexts, forcing distributed transactions and tight coupling.
Mixing domain events with integration events at the entity level, leaking infrastructure concerns into the model.
Ignoring eventual consistency: expecting cross-aggregate operations to complete synchronously within a transaction.

Wrong move: giving every CRUD screen a rich model -> the Data Mapper machinery costs more than the logic it protects and the project stalls -> instead reserve the domain model for genuinely complex areas and use Transaction Script or Active Record where the rules are thin.

Wrong move: letting application services read entity getters, compute the rule and write it back -> the model turns anemic and the rule re-appears in every handler until the copies diverge -> instead move the rule into the entity that owns the data as a command or Specification.

Wrong move: wiring whole object graphs together with ORM lazy associations to skip the mapping work -> N+1 queries and detached-state errors dominate at runtime -> instead load each use case's working set explicitly and size the aggregate to be the unit of loading and consistency.
